article_title: Reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages in breast cancer: from myeloid plasticity and tumor-promoting programs to CAR-macrophage therapy.
caption_title: Therapeutic targeting and reprogramming strategies within the macrophage axis of the breast cancer microenvironment
caption: (A) Disruption of monocyte recruitment, retention, and local expansion. Tumor- and stromal-derived CCL2, operating in concert with VEGF, drives the mobilization and transendothelial extravasation of circulating CCR2⁺ inflammatory monocytes into metastatic niches. Target inhibition of CCL2–CCR2 signaling impairs recruitment, whereas local retention and proliferation are sustained by secondary CCL3–CCR1 and CSF1–CSF1R signaling circuits. Cessation of monocyte blockade triggers an adaptive rebound in IL-6 and VEGF-A expression, driving compensatory angiogenesis and accelerated metastatic seeding. (B) Mechanisms and severe off-target liabilities of systemic TAM depletion. Broad depletion strategies using systemic CSF1/CSF1R-directed approaches include the anti-CSF1 antibody lacnotuzumab and CSF1R-directed agents such as pexidartinib and LY3022855. Clinical studies have identified agent- and regimen-specific hepatic safety concerns; the contribution of Kupffer-cell loss to these events remains unclear and may impair antitumor surveillance by depleting protective CD169⁺ lymph node macrophages. (C) Functional re-education and checkpoint-mediated phagocytosis enhancement. Epigenetic modulation (HDACi TMP195), localized activation of innate immune sensing (STING, TLR7/8 agonists, ferumoxytol), or NAMPT-targeted PROTAC degradation transforms immunosuppressive, hypoxic SPP1⁺ TAMs into cytotoxic, antigen-presenting (MHC-II⁺/iNOS⁺) effector states. Concurrently, targeted disruption of antiphagocytic checkpoints (CD47–SIRPα, CD24–Siglec-10, MHC I–LILRB1, and trastuzumab-induced B7-H4) overcomes phagocytic resistance, restoring HER2-targeted tumor cell engulfment and enhancing downstream T-cell recruitment. (D) Active macrophage engineering and microenvironmental ecosystem remodeling. Adoptive cell transfer of HER2-targeted CAR-macrophages (CAR-M) facilitates direct, targeted tumor engulfment, bystander immunosuppressive TAM reprogramming, and local CD8⁺ T-cell priming. Ecosystem remodeling is further optimized through localized cytokine delivery (IL-12/CXCL9), dual-aptamer non-genetic modifications, and metabolic reinforcement via SLC38A2-dependent glutamine utilization, restoring sustained functional fitness within nutrient-deprived tumor microenvironments

article_title: Reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages in breast cancer: from myeloid plasticity and tumor-promoting programs to CAR-macrophage therapy.
caption_title: Multi-stage orchestration of breast cancer progression, immune exclusion, and premetastatic niche conditioning by tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
caption: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) operate as principal signaling hubs within the breast tumor microenvironment (TME), driving primary tumor growth, invasion, vascular dissemination, extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics, and distant organ priming. (A) Inflammatory Support of Tumor Growth : TAMs sustain primary malignancy through a reciprocal CSF1–CSF1R trophic loop—where tumor-derived CSF1 expands TAM populations while TAMs deliver growth and survival factors back to tumor cells—and paracrine IL-6/JAK-STAT3 signaling that expands stem-like cancer cell populations. Concurrently, CD4⁺ T cell–derived IL-4 activates STAT6 signaling to reinforce pro-tumorigenic M2-like macrophage polarization. (B) EMT , Invasion , and Early Dissemination : Intravital paracrine loops (tumor CSF1 and macrophage EGF) direct cancer cell chemotaxis toward the vasculature. Reciprocal GM-CSF/CCL18 (PITPNM3) signaling stabilizes hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity (EMP), while specialized CD206⁺/TIE2⁺ TAMs facilitate early cancer cell escape from premalignant mammary lesions before invasive transformation. (C) Angiogenesis , TMEM Gateways , and Therapeutic Adaptation : TAM-derived VEGF-A and WNT7B drive the angiogenic switch from avascular to hypervascular states. Perivascular TIE2 high VEGFA high TAMs assemble within the Tumor Microenvironment of Metastasis (TMEM) tripartite structures (composed of a TAM, a MENA-expressing tumor cell, and an endothelial cell) to induce transient vascular permeability for tumor cell intravasation. Under chemotherapy stress (e.g., paclitaxel), VEGFR3⁺ TAMs drive lymphangiogenesis via the cathepsin–heparanase–VEGF-C pathway, whereas MRC1⁺ TIE2 high CXCR4 high TAMs promote post-treatment vascular remodeling. (D) ECM Remodeling and Physical/Metabolic Immune Exclusion : TAMs balance matrix degradation via invasive-front cathepsins with TGF-β1-dependent collagen deposition, generating a rigid fibrotic niche that mechanically restricts cytotoxic CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration. Simultaneously, TAMs divert arginine metabolism toward ornithine and proline synthesis, depleting essential amino acids required for effective T-cell effector function. (E) Premetastatic Cascade and Metastatic Niche Formation : Primary tumor-derived CCL2 recruits CCR2⁺ inflammatory monocytes to distant lungs, where tumor-induced CCL3/CCR1 signaling ensures their local retention as metastasis-associated macrophages (MAMs). These macrophages express α4 integrin to bind tumor VCAM1 (activating ezrin-PI3K-AKT survival signaling), secrete S100A4 to activate pulmonary fibroblasts, and enforce GM-CSF–STAT5–AHR-mediated immunosuppression to establish a receptive premetastatic microenvironment

article_title: The AMPK signaling pathway in cell metabolism and human diseases.
caption_title: AMPK activation by its upregulators and low energy level
caption: a Phosphorylation by upstream kinases is the main AMPK-activating event. Left, the regulation of AMPK phosphorylation can be adenylate-dependent (canonical regulation), resulting from changes in AMP:ATP or ADP:ATP ratios that are induced by a variety of energy stresses. Phosphorylation of AMPK at Thr172 is regulated by the upstream protein kinase LKB1, and dephosphorylation of AMPK at Thr172 is modulated by the protein phosphatases PP2A, PP2C, PP1-R6 and PPM1E. Right, AMPK is also activated in an adenylate-independent manner by calcium/CaMKK2/β and TAK1, ST-loop kinases. Some metabolic processes also activate AMPK, including DNA damage and repair, lysosomal damage, glucose sensing and glycogen sensing. b Left, AMPK is inactive under high energy levels. When glucose is abundant, it is metabolized by glycolysis to FBP, which binds to aldolase and the v-ATPase at the lysosomal surface, preventing the interaction of LKB1, AXIN, and AMPK on the lysosome. Right, AMPK is activated at the low energy level. In low glucose, the absence of FBP from aldolase causes a change in its interaction with the v-ATPase: Ragulator complex, which allows a ternary complex of LKB1, AXIN, and AMPK to bind to the v-ATPase and the Ragulator complex. The proximity of LKB1 and AMPK causes phosphorylation and activation of the latter. c Other novel metabolites that activate AMPK. Left, under calorie restriction conditions, lithocholic acid is elevated, which binds to TULP3 and activates sirtuins, which in turn deacetylate the V1E1 subunit of v-ATPase and inhibit v-ATPase, which, along with conformationally changed Ragulator, allows AXIN/LKB1 to translocate to the surface of the lysosome, where LKB1 phosphorylates and activates AMPK. Right, under fasting or high-fat diet conditions, long-chain fatty acid acyl-CoA (LCFA) allosterically activates AMPK by binding to the allosteric drug and metabolite site in a cell-free mechanism. Linoleic acid increases due to fasting or a ketogenic diet, and it binds to two hydrophobic pockets on the γ subunit of AMPK

caption_title: Realization of non-Hermitian model and topology
caption: a Exceptional phases on nonorientable manifolds . Under the shown boundary identifications, the free parameter space rectangle transforms into a Klein bottle, the nonorientable momentum manifold on which the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian is defined. b The matrices U 1 , U 2 , U E 1 , and U E 2 form a unitary 4 × 4 matrix that simulates the dynamics of a non-Hermitian 2 × 2 evolution operator T , with coupling to the environment implemented through ancilla modes 1 and 2. The components U 1 and U 2 correspond to tunable beam splitters and phase shifters acting within the system, while U E 1 and U E 2 couple the system to the environment, represented here by the ancilla modes. c Schematic of a single Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) unit, serving as the fundamental computational element of the programmable photonic circuit. The brown boxes represent 3-dB MMIs, and the circles with arrows denote the external and internal phase shifters controlling ϕ and θ , respectively. d An illustration of the experimental setup is shown, where the sizes of individual components have been adjusted for clarity. A 1550 nm pulsed diode laser (PDL 800-B) is employed as the light source. The polarization of the transmitted light is controlled to be in the TE mode using a three-paddle polarization controller. Two 1 × 12 MEMS optical switches are used in the system (Using eight of the channels). The input light is coupled into the first optical switch, allowing any of the eight operational modes or four additional test modes to be selected under computer control. The core of the system is an 8 × 8 silicon PIC comprising an array of 28 Mach-Zehnder Interferometers (MZIs) and 56 heating-electrodes. The PIC is controlled by one of eight current driver modules (Qontrol Ltd.) interfaced with the host computer running the GUI based on Python 3.11. The output light is coupled into the second optical switch and its intensity is measured using a Thorlabs PM400 power meter. During the measurement process, the second optical switch rapidly cycles through output modes 1 to 8 at each experimental step to acquire the full set of output intensities

caption_title: Overview of Cycle-Extractor(CE).
caption: CE takes as input, an amplicon graph generated using short-reads (e.g., from AA) or long-reads (e.g., from CoRAL). It applies a mixed-integer linear program to iteratively extract heaviest cycles from the graph (optimization step), and producing ordered traversals of edges (traversal step). The graph is updated by decreasing the copy number of the edges in the selected cycle, and the process is repeated until the amplification is explained.

caption_title: Overview of the scDaisyChain phasing algorithm.
caption: scDaisyChain reconstructs the parental X chromosome haplotypes and quantifies expression from the active and inactive X. (a) In Stage 1, heterozygous SNPs are encoded in a binary detection matrix, which is then used to construct a weighted graph where the edges represent co-expression frequency of a pair of alleles. Community leading eigenvector partitioning is used to separate the graph into two broad haplotypes, which are then further refined by removal of pairs of alleles where the REF and ALT segregate into the same haplotype. The graphing, partitioning and refinement are repeated iteratively until there is convergence to two haplotypes with no further refinement possible. (b) In stage 2, pairs of SNPs excluded from stage 1 are phased based on the concordance of their allelic expression with the active X identity of each cell. (c) The final haplotypes enable downstream analyses including cell type specific quantification of XCI escape, estimation of XCI skew and variant exposure analysis.

caption_title: a Physical appearance and system architecture
caption: b Dynamic color compensation and visualization examples. caption_title: Schematic overview of CoSyn-RNN.
caption: a Conceptual schematic, adapted from 9 , illustrating two intersecting low-error parameter regions for tasks A and B. The black dot denotes the initial parameter state, and the yellow dot denotes a shared low-error solution. The black arrow illustrates learning task A from scratch. The red-dashed arrow illustrates how sequentially learning task B without protecting task A’s solution can move the parameters out of task A’s lowerror region, resulting in catastrophic forgetting of task A. In contrast, the blue arrow illustrates how our model constrains subsequent parameter updates to remain within task A’s low-error region, thereby preserving performance on task A. b Schematic of the model architecture. Task inputs feed into the recurrent weights via the shared Win projection. The recurrent weights are optimized to preserve prior knowledge in task-dependent neuron groups (NG). The update rule permits connections from synaptically-consolidated groups into future learning, and connections into protected earlier groups are constrained and regularized, though not identically zero. Behavior is readout from the recurrent neurons via the task-cue-modulated projection W out ⊙ M ( t ). c Example trial from the FdGo task, illustrating the task input and target structure. article_title: Structural basis of H-NS-mediated temperature-dependent stimulation of initial growth in Escherichia coli
caption_title: Impact of the Rac prophage on temperature-dependent growth stimulation and comparative genomic mapping.
caption: (a) Temperature-dependent profiles of the specific growth rate at the onset of the logarithmic phase (μ at ODratio = 0.2) for E. coli MG1655 (filled circles) and W3110 type A (open circles). (b) Comparison of growth deceleration rates across temperatures for MG1655 and W3110 type A. In both (a) and (b), each data point represents the mean value derived from 12 independent colonies, with error bars indicating the standard deviation. (c) Comparative circular genome maps of MG1655 (left) and W3110 type A (right). Colored boxes indicate the positions and sizes (kb) of various prophage elements. The 23-kb Rac prophage (orange box) is present in the MG1655 genome but notably absent in W3110 type A, correlating with the lack of significant growth stimulation at 37°C in the latter strain.
